title: Airway management
summary: Plan every ICU intubation as a high-risk event: predict anatomical and physiological difficulty, preoxygenate properly (NIV or HFNC when hypoxaemic), choose haemodynamically safe induction drugs, use a video laryngoscope and bougie, follow a clear failed-airway plan to front-of-neck access, confirm with waveform capnography, and extubate safely.

topics.title: Airway assessment and preparation (anatomical and physiological)
topics.summary: Before every ICU intubation, score anatomical difficulty (MACOCHA), identify physiological risks (hypoxaemia, hypotension, acidosis, RV failure), and run a checklist with a team brief and a stated Plan A-B-C-D.

steps.title: Is intubation needed now?
steps.detail: Failure to protect airway, oxygenate or ventilate; anticipated course; procedural need. Call a senior early for predicted difficulty.

steps.title: Anatomical risk: MACOCHA
steps.detail: Mallampati III-IV (5), OSA (2), reduced cervical mobility (1), mouth opening < 3 cm (1), coma (1), severe hypoxaemia SpO2 < 80% (1), non-anaesthetist operator (1). Score ≥ 3 predicts difficult intubation.

steps.title: Physiological risk
steps.detail: Hypoxaemia, hypotension (SBP < 90, shock index > 0.9), severe metabolic acidosis, RV failure/pulmonary hypertension, raised ICP, full stomach.

steps.title: Resuscitate before induction
steps.detail: Preoxygenate (next topic); start noradrenaline if hypotensive or shock index high; consider bicarbonate/ventilation plan in severe acidosis (match minute ventilation after intubation).

steps.title: Equipment (STOP MAID / checklist)
steps.detail: Suction ×2, oxygen sources, BVM with PEEP valve, video and direct laryngoscopes, bougie, 2 tube sizes (7.0-8.0), second-generation SGA, scalpel-bougie-tube FONA kit, waveform capnography connected, drugs drawn and labelled.

steps.title: Brief
steps.detail: Roles (intubator, drugs, airway assistant with cricoid/BURP, monitor watcher, runner), verbalise Plan A (VL + bougie), Plan B (SGA), Plan C (face mask), Plan D (FONA) and the 'call out' SpO2.

steps.title: Ramp and head up
steps.detail: Ear-to-sternal notch alignment; 20-30° head-up (reverse Trendelenburg if spine precautions) improves preoxygenation and reduces aspiration.

tables.title: Physiologically difficult airway: risk and response

SBP < 90 mmHg before induction: vasopressor running first.
Severe metabolic acidosis with compensatory hyperventilation: apnoea can trigger arrest.

pitfalls.text: Intubating 'quickly' without a checklist at night.

pearls.text: INTUBE (29 countries, Indian centres included): 45% of ICU intubations had a major adverse event, mostly cardiovascular instability; cardiac arrest in 3%.
AIDAA recommends announcing 'Code D' (difficult airway emergency code) to summon help.

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **INTUBE (2021):** 2964 intubations; ≥ 1 major adverse peri-intubation event in 45.2% (cardiovascular instability 42.6%, severe hypoxaemia 9.3%, cardiac arrest 3.1%).
- **DAS critically ill 2018:** checklist, team brief, video laryngoscope availability, capnography, and a stepwise failed-airway plan.
- **ESICM 2024 Delphi:** consensus statements for the physiologically difficult airway.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Awake intubation in the ICU is rarely possible in agitated, hypoxaemic patients.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- The AIDAA 2016 ICU guideline was written for Indian practice and recommends checklists, video laryngoscopes where available and second-generation SGAs.
- Many Indian ICUs depend on residents for night intubations; MACOCHA awards a point to the non-anaesthetist operator: escalate early.

quiz.stem: In MACOCHA, which factor scores 5 points?
quiz.explanation: Mallampati III or IV is the heaviest weighted factor.

quiz.stem: A septic patient with SBP 82 mmHg needs intubation. Best preparation?
quiz.explanation: Treat hypotension before induction; use a reduced-dose, haemodynamically stable induction.

topics.title: Preoxygenation and apnoeic oxygenation
topics.summary: Preoxygenate for 3-5 min to an ETO2 ≥ 85-90%; use NIV in hypoxaemic patients (PREOXI), keep nasal oxygen during apnoea, and give gentle bag-mask ventilation between induction and laryngoscopy (PreVent).

steps.title: Preoxygenate
steps.detail: Head up 20-30°. Tight-fitting face mask with 15 L/min (or BVM with PEEP valve), or NIV (PEEP 5-8, pressure support 5-10, FiO2 1.0) in hypoxaemic patients; HFNC 60 L/min is an alternative. Target ETO2 ≥ 85-90% if measurable.

steps.title: Apnoeic oxygenation
steps.detail: Nasal cannula 10-15 L/min (or HFNC) left on throughout laryngoscopy.

steps.title: Bag-mask ventilation
steps.detail: Gentle BMV (low pressure, 10/min) with PEEP after induction reduces severe hypoxaemia.

steps.title: Stop at threshold
steps.detail: Abort the attempt if SpO2 falls to ~93% (or earlier in shunt); re-oxygenate with BMV or SGA before the next attempt.

redFlags.text: SpO2 < 93% despite NIV preoxygenation: shunt physiology, expect rapid desaturation.
Cannot preoxygenate (agitation): consider delayed sequence intubation with ketamine 1 mg/kg.

pitfalls.text: Removing NIV or HFNC to 'get ready' minutes before induction.

pearls.text: Delayed sequence intubation: ketamine (0.5-1 mg/kg) dissociation allows effective NIV preoxygenation in an agitated patient.

nodes.text: Planned intubation
Hypoxaemic (SpO2 < 93% on O2 or high FiO2 needs)?
NIV preoxygenation (PEEP 5-8, PS 5-10, FiO2 1.0) + nasal O2 for apnoea
Tight face mask 15 L/min or BVM with PEEP valve, 3-5 min + nasal O2
Patient tolerating?
Delayed sequence: ketamine 0.5-1 mg/kg, then NIV
Induce; gentle BMV until laryngoscopy

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **PREOXI (2024):** NIV preoxygenation reduced hypoxaemia (SpO2 < 85%) during intubation from 18.5% to 9.1% vs oxygen mask, with no increase in aspiration.
- **PreVent (2019):** bag-mask ventilation between induction and laryngoscopy halved severe hypoxaemia (10.9% vs 22.8%) without more aspiration.
- **AIDAA 2025:** nasal oxygen 10-15 L/min or HFNO during apnoea increases safe apnoea time.
consultantNotes.controversies: - HFNC vs NIV preoxygenation in severe hypoxaemia: NIV generally achieves better oxygen reserves; HFNC can stay on during laryngoscopy.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Ordinary nasal prongs at 15 L/min are cheap and nearly universal; use them for apnoeic oxygenation even where HFNC is not available.

quiz.explanation: NIV reduced hypoxaemia compared with an oxygen mask.

topics.title: Rapid sequence induction: drugs and technique
topics.summary: Use reduced-dose, haemodynamically safer induction (ketamine or etomidate in shock), full-dose rocuronium or succinylcholine, a video laryngoscope with bougie or stylet, and confirm with waveform capnography.

steps.title: Final check
steps.detail: Monitoring (SpO2, ECG, BP every 1-2 min or arterial line), capnography attached, suction on, drugs labelled, vasopressor ready.

steps.title: Induction agent
steps.detail: Shock: ketamine 0.5-1 mg/kg or etomidate 0.15-0.2 mg/kg. Stable: propofol 1-1.5 mg/kg or ketamine 1-2 mg/kg.

steps.title: Paralytic immediately after
steps.detail: Rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg or succinylcholine 1.5 mg/kg (actual body weight).

steps.title: Laryngoscopy
steps.detail: Video laryngoscope first-line (DEVICE); bougie or stylet for every attempt. Cricoid pressure optional; release if it worsens the view.

steps.title: Waveform capnography
steps.detail: Sustained ETCO2 waveform over ≥ 5 breaths. 'No trace = wrong place' (except in arrest with very poor CPR).

steps.title: Post-induction hypotension
steps.detail: Expect it: noradrenaline titration, small fluid bolus if responsive (routine fluid bolus did not prevent collapse: PREPARE II). Start sedation and analgesia promptly.

doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg in shock: 0.75 mg/kg ≈ 50 mg = 5 mL of 10 mg/mL

doseCards.dose: 1-2 mg/kg; 0.5-1 mg/kg if elderly or borderline BP
1-3 mcg/kg 3 min before induction; omit in shock

tables.title: Induction agents compared
rows: Usually maintains BP; can fall in catecholamine depletion

redFlags.text: No capnography trace: assume oesophageal intubation; remove the tube unless you can see it through the cords on VL.
Succinylcholine with hyperkalaemia, crush, burns > 24 h, denervation or prolonged immobility: risk of fatal hyperkalaemia.
SBP < 65 mmHg after induction: noradrenaline bolus/infusion now, check for tension pneumothorax or auto-PEEP.

pitfalls.text: Hyperventilating with the bag after intubation (auto-PEEP, hypotension).
Forgetting post-intubation sedation after short-acting induction with long-acting rocuronium (awareness).

pearls.text: With rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg, sugammadex 16 mg/kg can reverse within ~3 min, but in the ICU waking up is rarely a real rescue plan.

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **RSI trial (2025):** ketamine vs etomidate in 2365 critically ill adults: no difference in 28-day in-hospital mortality (28.1% vs 29.1%); cardiovascular collapse during intubation was more frequent with ketamine (22.1% vs 17.0%).
- **DEVICE (2023):** video laryngoscopy improved first-attempt success (85.1% vs 70.8%) vs direct laryngoscopy.
- **BOUGIE (2021):** bougie did not improve first-attempt success over tube + stylet overall.
- **PREPARE II (2022):** a 500 mL fluid bolus did not reduce cardiovascular collapse.
- **SCCM RSI guideline 2023:** evidence-based recommendations on induction agents, NMB choice and adjuncts in critically ill adults.
consultantNotes.controversies:
- Etomidate adrenal suppression: the RSI trial and meta-analyses show no clear mortality signal from a single dose.
- Cricoid pressure: unproven benefit, may worsen view.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Etomidate is available but not stocked everywhere; ketamine is cheap and universal.
- Video laryngoscopes (including Indian-made devices) are increasingly common but often limited to one per ICU; ensure it is charged and in the airway trolley.

options: Did not reduce mortality and caused more cardiovascular collapse

quiz.explanation: 1.2 mg/kg actual body weight gives intubating conditions in ~60 s.
After 24-48 h, burns cause receptor upregulation and risk of hyperkalaemia.

topics.title: Failed intubation and CICO (can't intubate, can't oxygenate)
topics.summary: Limit attempts, switch promptly between tube, SGA and face mask to oxygenate, call 'Code D', and perform scalpel-bougie-tube cricothyroidotomy without delay when all three fail.

steps.title: Call for help
steps.detail: Announce 'failed intubation', call 'Code D' / senior. Re-oxygenate with BMV (2-person, OPA/NPA) between attempts.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.detail: Position, full paralysis, external laryngeal manipulation, different blade or device, more experienced operator. Maximum 3 attempts at intubation (+1 by expert) while SpO2 is maintained.

steps.title: Second-generation SGA
steps.detail: Up to 3 attempts. If it works: stop and think (wake? intubate via SGA with fibreoptic? FONA?).

steps.title: Face mask
steps.detail: 2-person technique with adjuncts; ensure paralysis. AIDAA 2025: no fixed hierarchy between tube, SGA and mask; switch rapidly to whichever ventilates.

steps.title: Declare it
steps.detail: Ventilation fails by tube, SGA and mask: declare CICO. AIDAA 2025: complete ventilation failure (even if SpO2 still holds) is the trigger.

steps.title: Front-of-neck access
steps.detail: Scalpel-bougie-tube: extend neck, identify cricothyroid membrane (laryngeal handshake), transverse stab incision with No. 10 blade, rotate 90°, bougie, rail a 6.0 cuffed tube. Vertical skin incision first if membrane is impalpable.

redFlags.text: SpO2 falling below 80% with failing mask ventilation: prepare FONA immediately.
Repeated laryngoscopy attempts cause airway oedema and turn 'can't intubate' into 'can't oxygenate'.

pitfalls.text: Fixation on intubation while SpO2 falls.
Needle cricothyroidotomy without a high-pressure source (inadequate ventilation).
Missing paralysis: giving sugammadex reflexively in the ICU when waking is not realistic.

pearls.text: Mark the cricothyroid membrane with a pen (or ultrasound) before induction in predicted difficult airways.
Keep a FONA kit (No. 10 scalpel, bougie, 6.0 cuffed tube) on every airway trolley.

nodes.text: Intubation attempt fails
Call for help / 'Code D'; oxygenate by BMV
Oxygenation adequate (SpO2 maintained)?
Optimise and re-attempt (max 3 + 1 expert) with VL, bougie
Intubated: confirm capnography
Second-generation SGA (max 3 attempts)
SGA or mask ventilates?
Stop and think: wake, fibreoptic via SGA, or elective FONA
Declare CICO; ensure paralysis
Scalpel-bougie-tube cricothyroidotomy
Re-attempt successful?

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **AIDAA 2025:** guidance for failure of any primary airway plan (SGA, tube or mask); "Code D"; switch between tube, SGA and face mask without hierarchy; up to three attempts with these devices provided SpO2 remains ≥ 95%; complete ventilation failure triggers emergency cricothyroidotomy, preferably surgical.
- **DAS 2015 and DAS ICU 2018:** Plans A-D, scalpel-bougie-tube FONA as the recommended technique.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Surgical vs cannula techniques: cannula techniques have high failure rates in emergencies.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - AIDAA guidelines are designed for Indian hospitals and emphasise simple, cheap tools (bougie, scalpel, tube) available everywhere.

quiz.stem: According to AIDAA 2025, emergency cricothyroidotomy is triggered by:
options: Complete ventilation failure via tube, SGA and face mask
quiz.explanation: Complete ventilation failure, even if oxygenation is momentarily maintained.

quiz.stem: After a successful SGA rescue in a failed intubation, the next step is:
options: Stop and think about the safest definitive plan
quiz.explanation: Pause and choose: wake, fibreoptic through the SGA, or controlled FONA.

verify.reason: AIDAA 2025 abstract states up to three attempts while SpO2 ≥ 95%; DAS 2018 ICU states maximum 3 + 1 laryngoscopy attempts. Confirm the exact local protocol.

topics.title: Immediately after intubation
topics.summary: Confirm and secure the tube, set lung-protective ventilation matched to the patient's prior minute ventilation, treat hypotension, start analgosedation, check the chest X-ray and cuff pressure, and document the airway.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.detail: Waveform capnography, bilateral chest rise and breath sounds, SpO2 recovery.

steps.title: Secure and depth
steps.detail: Tube at ~21 cm (women) / 23 cm (men) at the teeth; tie or tape; cuff pressure 20-30 cmH2O with a manometer.

steps.title: Ventilator
steps.detail: Vt 6-8 mL/kg PBW, PEEP 5-8 (higher if hypoxaemic), FiO2 1.0 then titrate to SpO2 92-96%. In severe metabolic acidosis, match the pre-intubation minute ventilation (often rate 25-30). See module 8.

steps.title: Haemodynamics
steps.detail: Expect hypotension from induction, positive pressure and loss of sympathetic drive; titrate noradrenaline; exclude tension pneumothorax and auto-PEEP if BP crashes.

steps.title: Sedation and analgesia
steps.detail: Start analgesia-first sedation (fentanyl infusion + propofol); target RASS according to need (deeper if paralysed).

steps.title: Chest X-ray and gas
steps.detail: Tube tip 3-5 cm above carina; check for pneumothorax and NG position; ABG at 30 min. Insert NG/OG tube.

steps.title: Airway record
steps.detail: Grade of view, device, attempts, adjuncts, difficulty, and a 'difficult airway' alert on the bed and in the notes if relevant.

redFlags.text: Sudden hypotension and rising airway pressure: tension pneumothorax or auto-PEEP; disconnect briefly and examine.
Desaturation after intubation: DOPES (Displacement, Obstruction, Pneumothorax, Equipment, Stacking).

pitfalls.text: Leaving the patient paralysed without sedation.
Right main bronchus intubation (check depth and breath sounds).

pearls.text: Write the tube size and depth on the whiteboard; check it at every handover.

nodes.text: SpO2 or BP falls after intubation
Hand-bag with FiO2 1.0; briefly disconnect if pressures high
ETCO2 waveform present and tube depth correct?
Displaced tube: reposition or reintubate
Suction catheter passes freely?
Obstruction: suction, change tube if blocked
Unilateral absent breath sounds / no lung sliding?
Pneumothorax: decompress then drain
Check equipment, auto-PEEP (stacking), shock, bronchospasm, PE

consultantNotes.evidence: - DAS ICU 2018 includes post-intubation steps: confirm with capnography, plan ventilation, sedation, and handover of airway details.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Cuff manometers are often missing; a cheap aneroid cuff manometer prevents tracheal injury and micro-aspiration.

quiz.stem: Shortly after intubation, BP falls and airway pressures rise. First action?
options: Briefly disconnect the ventilator and assess for tension/auto-PEEP
quiz.explanation: Disconnection relieves breath stacking and helps diagnose tension.
20-30 cmH2O balances seal and mucosal perfusion.

quiz.stem: Correct tube tip on chest X-ray:
quiz.explanation: 3-5 cm above the carina with the head neutral.

topics.title: Planning and performing extubation
topics.summary: Extubate after a successful SBT when the patient can protect the airway; stratify risk, use a cuff leak test in high-risk patients, give steroids for a failed leak, use HFNC or NIV after extubation in high-risk patients, and be ready to reintubate.

steps.title: Readiness
steps.detail: Passed SBT (module 8), awake and following commands, adequate cough, secretions manageable (suction ≤ every 2 h), haemodynamically stable.

steps.title: Risk stratify
steps.detail: Low risk vs at-risk (known difficult airway, airway oedema, prolonged intubation, trauma to airway, obesity, failed previous extubation).

steps.title: Cuff leak test (at-risk only)
steps.detail: Volume-controlled ventilation: measure Vt with cuff inflated and deflated; leak < 110 mL (or < 10-12%) suggests risk of stridor.

steps.title: Steroids
steps.detail: Methylprednisolone 20 mg every 4 h for 4 doses (start ≥ 4 h before extubation).

steps.title: Extubate
steps.detail: Head up, preoxygenate on FiO2 1.0, suction mouth and tube, deflate cuff, remove at peak inspiration with positive pressure, apply O2 or HFNC/NIV.

steps.title: Support high-risk patients
steps.detail: HFNC or prophylactic NIV after extubation in high-risk patients (age > 65, cardiac disease, COPD, hypercapnia). See module 7.

steps.title: Treat promptly
steps.detail: Nebulised adrenaline, heliox if available, IV steroids, head up; NIV is not a cure; reintubate early (smaller tube) if worsening.

doseCards.role: Prevent post-extubation stridor after failed cuff leak
doseCards.dose: 20 mg every 4 h × 4 doses before extubation
1 mg in 4 mL NS (up to 5 mg undiluted)

redFlags.text: Stridor with rising work of breathing after extubation: senior, airway trolley, reintubation plan.
Delayed reintubation after failed extubation increases mortality.

pitfalls.text: Extubating a patient who cannot cough or has copious secretions despite passing the SBT.
Using rescue NIV to avoid reintubation in established post-extubation respiratory failure (associated with delayed reintubation and harm).

pearls.text: For a known difficult airway, consider extubation over an airway exchange catheter (DAS advanced algorithm).

nodes.text: Passed SBT
Awake, adequate cough, manageable secretions?
Not ready: address cough or secretions; reassess daily
At-risk airway (oedema, difficult airway, prolonged intubation)?
Cuff leak present?
Methylprednisolone 20 mg q4h × 4, then extubate with airway plan
Extubate; HFNC or NIV if high risk for respiratory failure
Observe closely; reintubate early if failing

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ATS/CHEST 2017:** suggests cuff leak testing in patients at high risk for post-extubation stridor and systemic steroids at least 4 h before extubation if the leak fails; suggests preventive NIV after extubation in high-risk patients.
- **DAS 2012:** low-risk and at-risk extubation algorithms.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Heliox is rarely available in India; rely on adrenaline nebulisation, steroids and early reintubation.

quiz.stem: A cuff leak volume suggesting risk of stridor is:
quiz.explanation: < 110 mL (or < 10-12% of delivered Vt) is commonly used.

quiz.stem: If the cuff leak test fails in a high-risk patient, ATS/CHEST suggests:
quiz.explanation: Systemic steroids reduce post-extubation stridor and reintubation.

quiz.stem: After extubation of a 72-year-old with COPD and hypercapnia, best support is:
quiz.explanation: Preventive NIV reduces reintubation in high-risk (especially hypercapnic) patients.

drugs.name: Ketamine
drugs.indications: Induction in haemodynamically unstable patients, asthma, sepsis; analgosedation.
drugs.adultDose: Induction 1-2 mg/kg IV (0.5-1 mg/kg in shock). Analgosedation 0.1-0.5 mg/kg/h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 50 mg/mL in 10 mL vials (also 10 mg/mL). For induction draw 200 mg to 20 mL = 10 mg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Can still cause hypotension in catecholamine-depleted patients; tachycardia, hypertension, emergence reactions, raised secretions. Raised ICP concerns are no longer considered a contraindication.

drugs.name: Etomidate
drugs.indications: Induction when cardiovascular stability is needed.
drugs.cautions: Single dose transiently suppresses adrenal 11-beta-hydroxylase; myoclonus; no analgesia.

drugs.name: Propofol
drugs.indications: Induction in haemodynamically stable patients; sedation after intubation.
drugs.adultDose: Induction 1-2 mg/kg (0.5-1 mg/kg or less in elderly or unstable). Sedation 0.5-4 mg/kg/h.
drugs.preparationIndia: 1% (10 mg/mL) in 20 mL and 50 mL vials.
drugs.cautions: Dose-related hypotension and myocardial depression; avoid full doses in shock.

drugs.name: Fentanyl
drugs.indications: Blunting the pressor response (head injury, aortic dissection, ACS); analgesia after intubation.
drugs.adultDose: Pre-induction 1-3 mcg/kg (omit or reduce in shock). Infusion 0.5-2 mcg/kg/h.
drugs.cautions: Hypotension by removing sympathetic drive; chest wall rigidity with rapid large doses.

drugs.name: Rocuronium
drugs.indications: RSI paralysis (preferred where succinylcholine is contraindicated).
drugs.adultDose: RSI 1.2 mg/kg IV (actual body weight); onset 45-60 s; duration 45-70 min.
drugs.preparationIndia: 10 mg/mL, 5 mL vials (50 mg). Store refrigerated (or check room-temperature shelf life).
drugs.cautions: Long duration if you cannot intubate: have sugammadex available. Anaphylaxis is rare.

drugs.name: Succinylcholine (suxamethonium)
drugs.indications: RSI when rapid offset is valuable and no contraindication.
drugs.adultDose: 1.5 mg/kg IV (actual body weight); onset 45 s; duration 8-10 min.
drugs.cautions: Contraindicated with hyperkalaemia, prolonged immobility (> 48-72 h), burns or crush > 24-48 h, denervation (stroke, spinal injury, GBS, neuromuscular disease), malignant hyperthermia history. Bradycardia with repeat doses.

drugs.name: Sugammadex
drugs.indications: Reversal of rocuronium (or vecuronium); immediate reversal in a can't-intubate situation when waking is a realistic plan.
drugs.adultDose: 16 mg/kg IV for immediate reversal after 1.2 mg/kg rocuronium; 2-4 mg/kg for routine reversal.
drugs.preparationIndia: 100 mg/mL, 2 mL vials. Expensive; keep in the airway trolley.
drugs.cautions: Reversal does not fix an obstructed airway; anaphylaxis; bradycardia.

drugs.name: Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)
drugs.indications: Prevent or treat peri-intubation hypotension (start before induction if SBP < 90 or shock index > 0.9).
drugs.adultDose: Infusion 0.05-0.3 mcg/kg/min; push-dose 4-8 mcg aliquots from a 4-16 mcg/mL syringe (specialist use).
drugs.preparationIndia: 4 mg in 50 mL (80 mcg/mL) for infusion; push-dose syringe 1 mL of 80 mcg/mL diluted to 10 mL = 8 mcg/mL.
drugs.cautions: Label push-dose syringes clearly; dilution errors are a known hazard.
drugs.verify: Push-dose vasopressors are not addressed by the guidelines cited; use local protocol.

drugs.name: Methylprednisolone
drugs.indications: Prevention of post-extubation stridor in patients with a failed cuff leak test.
drugs.adultDose: 20 mg IV every 4 h for 4 doses before extubation (start ≥ 4 h, ideally 12 h, before extubation).
drugs.preparationIndia: 40 mg, 125 mg, 500 mg and 1 g vials.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (nebulised)
drugs.adultDose: 1 mg (1 mL of 1 mg/mL) in 4 mL NS nebulised, or up to 5 mL of undiluted 1 mg/mL; may repeat.
drugs.cautions: Tachycardia; rebound swelling; prepare for reintubation.
drugs.verify: Nebulised adrenaline doses for adults vary between protocols.
